newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 10.4 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said on Wednesday program trading averaged 10.4 percent of its average daily volume of 468 million shares, or 48.9 million shares, during the week of November 18-22.
Buy programs accounted for a daily average 31.5 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 17.4 million shares.
In all markets, program trading during the week of Nov. 18-22 averaged 76.7 million shares a day
During the previous week, program trading accounted for 11.1 percent of the average daily volume.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, First Options conducted most of its program activity for its own account. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers executed all or most of their program activity for customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 59.6 percent to the total during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 14.3 percent.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1.0 million or more, the NYSE said.
